component_findings.abstraction_ceremony: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: Reusable abstractions such as types, interfaces/traits/generics or equivalent mechanisms can be declared and consumed without excessive scaffolding. Evidence basis: Inspected Zig micro-benchmark programs (mb00-mb11) and adversarial programs under template/programs/zig. | mb03.zig core arithmetic kernel (workload()) is compact (~15 lines), comparable in density to C/Rust equivalents. | Program harness (main()) requires manual buffer allocation and std.fmt.bufPrint for every printed line, adding verbosity versus higher-level languages. | Explicit std.Io.Threaded plumbing and io() handle passing add boilerplate lines versus e.g. Go's fmt.Println or Rust's println!. | No unnecessary copies observed; small structs returned by value; slices/arrays used directly. | Adversarial programs (ADV-*) are short (200-900 bytes) with explicit type annotations required by Zig's strict comptime/type system.

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic mandatory ceremony for the same kinds of ordinary programs. Do not reuse raw LOC/bytes/tokens as the score and do not reward external libraries.

component_findings.consistency_regular_forms: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Similar concepts use regular forms with few special-case spellings or context-dependent surface rules. Evidence basis: Reviewed naming, structure, comments, and control flow of Zig micro and adversarial benchmark sources. | Code uses clear identifiers (s_add, s_xor, s_mul, s_div, workload, Result) and doc-style comments referencing spec sections, aiding comprehension. | Explicit types on every variable make data flow and semantics unambiguous at the cost of extra text. | Error handling via '!' return types and 'try' is visible and linear, avoiding hidden exception control flow. | while-loop-with-continue-expression syntax is idiomatic Zig but less immediately readable to newcomers than for-range loops in Python/Go/Rust. | Low-level I/O setup intermixes infrastructure concerns with program logic, slightly reducing readability of main(). | Comptime/generic-heavy adversarial cases remain readable due to Zig's explicit style (no operator overloading obscuring behavior).
